text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment relies on lifestyle changes, blood sugar monitoring, and medications or insulin when needed.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, blood sugar monitoring, and medications or insulin when needed

list.snippet: Diet: Eat healthy foods like lean proteins, non-starchy vegetables, and whole grains while reducing high-sugar foods.
Exercise: Get regular physical activity, such as 30 minutes a day or 150 minutes a week, to lower blood sugar and help with weight loss.
Monitoring: Check blood sugar levels regularly with a glucometer as directed by your doctor.
Metformin: Often the first oral medicine prescribed; it lowers sugar made by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.
GLP-1 receptor agonists: Injectable drugs that boost insulin release and can help with weight loss.
SGLT2 inhibitors: Pills that help the kidneys remove excess sugar through urine.
Sulfonylureas: Older oral medications that tell the pancreas to make more insulin.
Insulin: Injections or pump therapy used when other medicines do not control blood sugar enough.
